newsitem.title: FRANCE: Maghreb gas pipeline to start within weeks.
newsitem.headline: Maghreb gas pipeline to start within weeks.

text.p: The Maghreb gas pipeline linking Algeria's main Hassi R'mel field to European markets will start commercial operations within two or three weeks, Algeria's Energy and Mining Minister said on Sunday.

"The last technical tests are running normally and this will allow the inauguration of the commercial canalisation in Algeria in two or three weeks," said Amar Makhloufi, quoted by the official Algerian news agency APS.

The 48-inch pipeline running to Spain and then Portugal will have a capacity of 9.5 billion cubic metres (bcm) a year when it goes on stream. Its capacity may be expanded in a second phase to 18.5 bcm a year to supply thirsty European markets in France and Germany.
Makhloufi held talks on Sunday in Algiers with junior German foreign minister Werner Hoyer on boosting cooperation between Algeria and Germany, including in the energy sector, said APS.
The gas pipeline, built at cost of some $2.0 billion, threads through southern Algeria to Morocco and runs 45 km (28 miles) offshore before it reachs Spain.
